reason: Measured and reproduced exactly. At every two-pane width the two grid tracks begin at the identical y and the first ink in each does not: owner-flight .b-who top 230.89 / baseline 242.89 against .b-measureHead top 250.89 / baseline 261.89 at 1024, 1152, 1280 and 1440 - a flat 20px, invariant across the band. The audience desk artifact is the same at 108.39 vs 128.39, the sheet at 108.39 vs 128.39 on screen and 41 vs 61 under emulateMedia('print'), so it lands on the keepsake too. The cause is exactly as stated: .b-measureHead carries margin: var(--gap-item) 0 0, and --gap-item is 20px; the margin collapses out of the anonymous wrapper measure() returns and stops at the column box, so it becomes a pure 20px indent of the whole right column. Below 1024 and on the phone that margin is doing real work - it is the only separation between .b-gapNote and the head - but at desk and on paper there is nothing above it in that column for it to separate from. The offset has no system behind it: nothing in the left column sits at 250.9 (.b-num top is 267.69), and the gap between the bottom of MARA & FINN (247.7) and the top of DAYS AWAY (250.9) is 3.2px, which is the definition of a near-miss rather than a stagger. Both objects are Geist Mono uppercase micro-labels one size step apart (12/16.8 and 11/15.4), so the eye reads them as the same typographic species and expects the grid's own promise to be kept. I checked the alternative reading the brief asked for - that these are not peers and are not meant to align - and rejected it: hierarchy here is already carried by ink (full vs 62%) and size, which is this palette's stated method, and the head's association downward to its count lane is positional and unchanged by the fix (the 16px gap to .b-measure moves with it). Screenshotted before and after at 1440: before is a stagger with nothing to justify it, after is one clean top line across the page, which is what Linear or Stripe would ship. Simulated at 1024/1152/1280/1440, on the sheet, in print media and in a rendered A4 PDF: the correction is a 20px lift of the right column, page height unchanged in the fixed desk frame, no clipping, no overflow, nothing else moves. Confirmed inert where the margin earns its keep - phone at 390 and owner-flight at 768 are byte-identical before and after - and it does not touch the 'days back' head in .b-backWrap, which needs its 20px. Neither gate is restated or broken: interaction-check's two uses of .b-measureHead are relative deltas, and audit.mjs never reads its position.
sharpenedFix: The proposed selector is wrong and would be a silent no-op: .b-measureHead's parent is the anonymous div measure() returns, not .b-plan, and at desk/print the column is a bare div with no .b-plan class at all. Use the column's first block instead. In b.css, inside the existing @media (min-width: 1024px) block: [data-medium="full"] .b-two > * > *:first-child > .b-measureHead { margin-top: 0 }. For the sheet the boundary is the container query, not a width, so add the pair inside the existing @container (min-width: 600px) rule: .b-print .b-two > * > *:first-child > .b-measureHead { margin-top: 0 }. Cleaner still, if render-b.js is in play: give measure()'s wrapper a class (.b-measureWrap) and scope both rules to .b-measureWrap > .b-measureHead, which says what it means and cannot be broken by a future reparent. Do NOT put the zero in the base rule or in the >=701px block - at 768 the field is one wide track and the 20px is the only air between the gap note and the head; I measured that regression (head 647.77 -> 627.77) with an unscoped selector. Take the margin to 0, not to 40: at 0 the baselines fall 1px apart, which is the correct optical result for a 12px and an 11px label on the same leading, and a 40px stagger would only be a louder version of the same unjustified offset.
